title: My AI built game reached Kongregate's Featured Games. Player tests still found what my prompts missed.
author: thecrownforge
selftext:
I make Crownforge, a browser kingdom builder. I design the game systems, characters, story and player flow. I use LLMs to help make the code and art.



On November 21, I found the game first in Kongregate's Featured Games section. I am happy about that, but I do not know why it was placed there. It also does not mean the game is finished.



My loop has been simple:



1. I describe the feature and the choices I want players to make.

2. AI helps build a version of it.

3. I play it and watch where real players get lost or stop.

4. I change the feature and test again.



AI can make a screen work quickly. It cannot tell me whether a new player understands the screen or wants to come back tomorrow. That has been the hard part.



If you use AI in game development, how do you decide that the first 10 minutes are good enough for new players? What do you measure, and what do you still have to watch yourself?



If you want to see the game I mean: [https://www.kongregate.com/en/games/Crownforge/crownforge-legacy-of-the-first-flame](https://www.kongregate.com/en/games/Crownforge/crownforge-legacy-of-the-first-flame)
